note: RM-005 C1 t5 pixel oracle: the five room textures that reach the GPU through
three/texture_cache.js, rendered from their authored file and from their
KTX2/ETC1S transcode through the same geometry, camera and sampler state at
1:1, and differenced in the framebuffer.
THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT ENDED THE SPRINT'S SECOND HALF.
RM-004 B5 deferred these five - it said seven, but two of them turned out to
be Skybox's and never used the cache at all - on the grounds that
acquireTexture hands out a Texture clone synchronously and cannot hold a
CompressedTexture. C1 removed that obstacle: an empty CompressedTexture is
handed out and cloned exactly as before, and the decoded payload is adopted
into the master and every live clone when the transcode lands. It worked,
and tests/browser/gpu-memory.test.js proves the part that mattered - two
clones differing in repeat still cost one GPU upload.
Then the oracle was pointed at the textures it had been built for, and four
of the five fail B4's 3.0 codec gate outright. Two fail by more than double.
THE FIFTH IS THE INTERESTING ONE. walllightmap.png passes on absolute error -
RMS 1.269, nothing off by more than 8 - and fails on the measure that fits
it. It is a hand-painted greyscale vignette spanning bytes 232 to 253, so its
entire dynamic range is 21 levels. 1.269 is 6.0% of that range and its worst
pixel is 23.8% of it. Judged against its own content it is the MOST damaged
of the five: hardwood's 7.441 is 2.9% of a full-range image. An absolute gate
is the wrong instrument for a low-contrast texture, and this is the case that
shows it.
THE QUALITY SWEEP, run before concluding, because B5 chose qualityLevel 128
out of a possible 255 and a gate failure at one setting is not a codec
verdict. It is: at maximum quality hardwood is still 1.8x the gate and
light_brick 2.8x, for nearly double the file. UASTC would fix it and runs
about 5.7x source on this catalog, against 320 KB of public-total headroom.
SO THE CACHE CHANGE WAS REVERTED RATHER THAN SHIPPED. It is correct and it
was tested, and it has no consumer: every texture behind it refuses the only
codec the project can afford. Machinery with no consumer is a liability, and
the finding is worth more than the code - the blocker was never the binding
constraint. These are detailed, tiled room surfaces, and they would have
refused ETC1S with any cache at all.
WHAT THIS RAISES ABOUT B5, and it is not settled here: B5 encoded 18 model
textures gating only on disk and VRAM, and never rendered one. If ETC1S is
this destructive on wood grain and brick at 512x512, some of those 18 are
likely degraded too. Re-measuring needs the sources, which are in git
history rather than in the tree. Recorded in the roadmap as a finding.
Columns are absolute per-channel differences over RGB, 0-255. pctOver8 is
the share of channels differing by more than 8, which is roughly where a
difference stops being arithmetic and starts being visible.
